newsitem.title: ITALY: SOCCER-PARMA PREVENT JUVENTUS WINNING ITALIAN TITLE.
newsitem.headline: SOCCER-PARMA PREVENT JUVENTUS WINNING ITALIAN TITLE.

text.p: Parma prevented Juventus from clinching their 24th Serie A title in front of their home fans on Sunday when they held the European champions to a hard-fought 1-1 draw at Turin's Delle Alpi Stadium.

But the draw merely delayed the Juventus party. The European Cup finalists kept a six-point lead over second-placed Parma and need only draw in one of their last two matches to lift their second "scudetto", or little shield, in three seasons.

The visitors looked the better side early on and were rewarded in the 29th minute when Juve's French playmaker Zinedine Zidane deflected a shot by Argentine Nestor Sensini past his own goalkeeper, Angelo Peruzzi.
But Juventus drew level 12 minutes later through a Nicola Amoruso penalty awarded after Italy striker Christian Vieri was fouled by fellow international Fabio Cannavaro.
Parma players erupted in protest at the decisionl along with their coach Carlo Ancelotti, who was shown a red card.
The draw kept Parma two points ahead of Internazionale, held 1-1 at Roma, to keep alive their hopes of taking part in next season's European Cup.
Elsewhere, Samdporia's long-dormant attack came alive to beat Udinese 4-0 in a key showdown for a spot in next season's UEFA Cup.

The win gave the Genoa club sole possession of fifth place on 49 points, one fewer than Lazio who came back to draw 2-2 at AC Milan to grab a point vital to their UEFA Cup hopes. Four Italian clubs qualify for the tournament.
Perugia, struggling to avoid relegation, triumphed 4-1 at relegated Reggiana to pull level on 34 points with Cagliari and Piacenza, who drew 1-1.
Two of those three teams are likely to drop into the second division with bottom club Reggiana and Verona, who became the second club condemned to relegation when they drew 1-1 draw with Atalanta.
